Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - Neptune Analytics

Hi Ava / Chris,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning - great discussion. As promised, a concise recap of what we heard and the key open items for pricing / sizing so we can put together a formal proposal.

Call highlights / current state:
- Production usage today: ~200M tokens / month across two models (inference + reranking).
- Peak runbook: 30-45 min bursts with higher concurrency during US mornings.
- Latency requirement: 95th <= 250ms for single-turn generation workloads.

Projected growth & targets:
- Expected ramp to ~1B tokens / month in 6 months, with potential to 2B+ in 12 months if pilot successful.
- Target unit economics: looking to hit roughly $600-600 per 1M tokens (open to trade-offs on latency vs cost).

Sizing / architecture signals we need from you:
1) Preferred GPU family (H100 preferred for throughput / NVLink + 80GB models, A100 as a cost trade-off).
2) Reserved capacity size target (ballpark: 4 GPUs / 8 GPUs / 16 GPUs).
3) Throughput targets in tokens/sec and concurrency (e.g., 2k tokens/sec sustained, 5k tokens/sec burst).

Next steps from Redwood (what we’ll do):
- Internal sizing & cost model and an initial pricing proposal (will include per-1M token unit economics).
- Perf benchmark plan and pilot proposal (30-day canary with a small reserved footprint).
- Draft contract/commit options for 12/24 month reserved capacity.

Attachments: Neptune-usage-estimates.xlsx (you shared during the call), redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf (pricing assumptions).

Can you confirm the preferred GPU family and an initial target for reserved size + desired throughput? If you want, we can also run a short perf test next week to validate throughput assumptions.

Thanks - talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole

- Current steady-state is closer to ~500M tokens/month (we underreported earlier).

Chris - perfect, thanks for the clarity. Based on the updated volumes (500M current, up to 2B peak) we sketched two initial sizing options for you to consider:

Option A (Performance-first):
- Reserved: 8x NVIDIA H100 (80GB)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~2,000-3,000 tokens/sec for typical prompt mixes with batching and KV caching enabled
- Good headroom for bursts and multi-model routing
- Rough list indicative price: $X/month reserved (see attached spreadsheet for assumptions) -> roughly maps to ~$650 per 1M tokens at ~70% sustained utilization.

Option B (Cost-first):
- Reserved: 4x NVIDIA A100 (80GB)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~900-1,200 tokens/sec
- Better list price; higher risk of saturation during marketing spikes without autoscaling/bursting to on-demand
- Maps to ~$900-1,100 per 1M tokens depending on burst mix and cache hit rates.

Notes on unit economics assumptions:
- Numbers above assume continuous batching, prefix/KV caching of common prompts, and steady-state utilization.
- We normalize to a $/1M tokens figure by dividing monthly cost of reserved capacity and estimated on-demand overage by expected token volume.
- Pilot can be used to calibrate actual cache hit rates and reduce uncertainty.

I’m attaching an initial sizing + pricing workbook (initial-sizing-and-pricing.xlsx) and a more detailed set of assumptions in the pricing PDF. Neha, Marcus - please flag any technical sizing tweaks.

If this looks ok, I’ll put together a draft proposal with a 30-day pilot option, 12-month reserved commitment pricing, and terms for scaling up mid-commit. We can set a call early next week to review.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Chris / Ava,

Quick technical addendum with benchmark assumptions and what to expect from the two sizing options:

Benchmarks (representative):
- 8x H100 cluster (NVLink / high interconnect): ~2.5k tokens/sec sustained for typical generation model (single-turn, 2k context) when using 64-128 token batching windows and KV cache for session-based traffic. 95th latency ~200-260ms.
- 4x A100 cluster: ~1.0k tokens/sec sustained under similar batching assumptions, 95th latency ~300-420ms under burst.

Caching & batching impact:
- Prefix/KV caching can reduce token compute by ~20-40% depending on prompt reuse.
- Continuous batching improves GPU efficiency but increases tail latency slightly; we tune per-route SLOs.

Operational notes:
- For marketing event bursts we recommend a small burst pool (on-demand) to handle 2-4x baseline traffic spikes, combined with autoscale policies and model fallbacks.
- We’ll instrument token-level cost telemetry so you can validate $/1M tokens during the pilot.

Attaching perf-bench-h100-8gpu.pdf with representative traces and latency distributions.

- Neha
